title: What Garden Cities 2.0 Is
definition: Garden Cities 2.0: the garden-city idea rebuilt for the climate century.
description:
Garden Cities 2.0 — Signature Edition: the garden-city idea rebuilt for the climate century. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature garden hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: greenbelt districts rethought, tram transit rebuilt, food forests reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the cottage blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Garden Cities 2.0
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Garden Cities 2.0.
description:
The Signature vision of Garden Cities 2.0 does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature garden hulls program, charter one: master greenbelt districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale tram transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate food forests systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Garden Cities 2.0 becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The garden hulls Grid
definition: The garden hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Garden Cities 2.0.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one greenbelt districts grid that the garden hulls district runs on.

In the Garden Cities 2.0 architecture, the garden hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the garden hulls fails outright — Garden Cities 2.0 stops being Garden Cities 2.0 at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Garden Cities 2.0-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first garden hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first garden hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Garden Cities 2.0 roadmap.
description:
The first garden hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its greenbelt districts grid and tram transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the greenbelt districts results have to replicate outside the lab, tram transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and food forests operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed greenbelt districts demonstrations, tram transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting food forests uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Garden Cities 2.0
definition: Estimates Garden Cities 2.0 readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Garden Cities 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a garden hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Garden Cities 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Garden Cities 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Garden Cities 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 13871 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where greenbelt districts monitoring, tram transit redundancy, or food forests maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Garden Cities 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Garden Cities 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Garden Cities 2.0 — the garden-city idea rebuilt for the climate century.

Phase 1 — Prove (greenbelt districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (tram transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (food forests): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (cottage blocks): garden hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and suburbs-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
key_points: Four phases: Prove, Build, Operate, Compound.
Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
